scene: First encounter with Wall-E, an ordinary low round robot vacuum in living-room hallway. Neet has planted all four fine paws in a stiff blocking stance directly ahead of robot, head low and very serious, leaving safe space before bumper. The round cleaner is angled slightly to go around him. Buddy follows just behind/alongside robot, nose tipped inquisitively toward its side brush as if giving it a tour, not biting. Two dogs full bodies, clearly distinct, elongated Buddy with real leg clearance, tiny Neet nub. Plain hardwood floor and sunroom doorway beyond, no humans, no logos/readable text, no face on robot. Humor from official blockade versus friendly escort. Entire actual scene drawn with credible perspective and contact, robot smaller than dogs.
placement_after: “Observe the commander defending the hallway. His colleague appears to be giving the invader a tour.”
alt_text: Neet blocks the robot’s route while Buddy appears to give the invader a tour.

arguments.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: fully drawn one-scene storyboard rough for Neet & Buddy Chronicles, not finished art. Landscape on warm ivory, monochrome graphite pencil, fully drawn actual dogs and setting, not diagram or stick figures. Single scene, no collage, no lettering. Restrained observational editorial humor, no exaggerated cartoon anatomy. Show connected neck, shoulder, spine, ribcage, pelvis, four owned limbs, credible floor support and coherent occlusion. Neet is tan/golden-fawn with a very short SMOOTH coat, cream muzzle/chin and irregular chest bib, modest rounded head, projecting tapering muzzle, huge broad-rooted cupped triangular ears, fine long legs below a full narrow torso, a tiny near-flush rump nub only. No long tail, shag, high white socks, black saddle, giant eyes or puppy head. Buddy has a full moderately elongated continuous charcoal close-coated torso, deep chest, visible neck and genuine leg clearance on substantial legs. Modest projecting muzzle, cream moustache/beard, light curved brows, tan chest fields flanking dark throat, pale lower legs/feet, softly pendant ears. No floor-length body shag, square generic terrier, dachshund-short legs or oversized head. Human appearances if visible are provisional story design, no claimed likeness. Actual selected original photographs govern only visible anatomy; generated model supplies provisional pen/wash style, never anatomy authority. Uncalibrated photos establish no fixed proportions/relative scale, weight, ancestry, motion timing, psychology or exact palette. N35 excludes anatomy; B08 styling only and not used; B25 unavailable; B30 supplemental resting evidence only and not used. Multiple encodings of one exposure count once. B04/B24 one exposure, only B04 here. Do not copy photo backgrounds. No costume/collar/extra objects unless specified by actual scene. Draw clear contour/support construction and complete room staging for inspection.
Draw a MONOCHROME staging rough, no watercolor finish yet. Body coats smooth with no long fur hatching; only Buddy face and ears furnished.
Actual scene S045: First encounter with Wall-E, an ordinary low round robot vacuum in living-room hallway. Neet has planted all four fine paws in a stiff blocking stance directly ahead of robot, head low and very serious, leaving safe space before bumper. The round cleaner is angled slightly to go around him. Buddy follows just behind/alongside robot, nose tipped inquisitively toward its side brush as if giving it a tour, not biting. Two dogs full bodies, clearly distinct, elongated Buddy with real leg clearance, tiny Neet nub. Plain hardwood floor and sunroom doorway beyond, no humans, no logos/readable text, no face on robot. Humor from official blockade versus friendly escort. Entire actual scene drawn with credible perspective and contact, robot smaller than dogs.
Input roles: Image1 N19: Neet side body, fine legs, full trunk, near-flush nub; head turned/far legs overlap. Image2 N29: Neet frontal standing chest and legs; foreshortened body, tail hidden. Image3 B29: Buddy lateral torso and tail, blurred stride; no neutral ratios/timing. Image4 B04: Buddy tidy photographed face/ears, chest and substantial legs; grass hides toes, torso foreshortened. Use smooth charcoal wash bounded by continuous natural contours with NO LONG FUR STROKES. Keep tan chest patches and pale lower legs. Hair strands belong only to Buddy’s eyebrows, moustache, beard and pendant ear furnishings, as seen in original reference photographs. Do not change any limb position or skull/body proportions. Preserve every box, paw contact, face, tail, object, camera position and color in this scene. Pale legs have long dangling hair strokes: suppress to short coat with only subtle toe furnishings.
